title: Advanced Professional Certificate Course in Comparative Public Administration
description: Embark on a global journey in public administration, from understanding historical influences to navigating bureaucratic dynamics, policy shaping, and the intricacies of global governance.
longDescription: This comprehensive course spans Comparative Public Administration, delving into historical contexts, bureaucratic structures, and policy dynamics. Explore the governance landscape, evaluating its measures, and understanding the intricate relationship between politics and administration in shaping development. The curriculum extends to global perspectives, analyzing administrative patterns, and assessing impacts on governance and development worldwide.
courseDetails: This course offers a holistic understanding of Comparative Public Administration, bureaucracy, policy analysis, and global public administration. From assessing criticisms of bureaucracy to analyzing the impact of mass media on public opinion, participants gain versatile insights into governance structures and policy landscapes. After the successful completion of this course, you will understand the following; Navigating the Historical Odyssey of Public Administration: ⦁ Explain the historical context and key events that have influenced the evolution of public administration in various countries. ⦁ Identify the significant issues and challenges faced by early public administration systems. ⦁ Analyze the impact of historical events, such as wars, revolutions, and social movements, on the development of public administration. ⦁ Understand Comparative administration. ⦁ Understand the governance along with its measures. Comparative Public administration growth and methods: ⦁ Understand Comparative Public Administration, its objectives and elements. ⦁ Define bureaucracy and understand its key features, including a hierarchical structure, rules and regulations, and specialisation of tasks. ⦁ Understand the classic bureaucratic model and its main principles. ⦁ Assess the criticisms of bureaucracy. ⦁ Analyse the power dynamics in bureaucratic organisations and understand how they can impact decision-making and policy implementation. ⦁ Explore the relationship between bureaucracy and political development. ⦁ Understand how change and innovation can be introduced in bureaucratic organisations. Comparative Public Policy and development: ⦁ Evaluate the effectiveness of public policies using various methods, including cost-benefit analysis, outcome evaluation, and process evaluation. ⦁ Understand and analyse the informal processes and actors that influence public policy-making. ⦁ Analyse the role of mass media in shaping public opinion and influencing policy-making. ⦁ Analyze the rhetoric and statements of political leaders and assess their impact on public policy. ⦁ Understand the role of special interest groups in shaping public policy and analyze the ways in which these groups exert influence. ⦁ Understand and apply different models of decision-making, including the rational model, incremental model, bounded rationality model, and consensus-building models. ⦁ Understand the relationship between politics and administration in shaping development, and analyze the ways in which this relationship affects the implementation of public policy. Global Ethics and Public Service: ⦁ Understand the concept and significance of global public administration and recognise global challenges. ⦁ Identify, analyse, and compare common administrative patterns in public administration worldwide. ⦁ Analyse administrative systems in developing countries, evaluating their impacts on governance and development. ⦁ Recognise and describe essential public administration institutions and their roles. ⦁ Comprehend the importance of administrative procedures and their establishment, implementation, and improvement. ⦁ Describe the structure and functions of public administration and assess variations. ⦁ Compare and evaluate the structural and functional differences in public administration between the US and Sweden. ⦁ Explore the roles of institutional channels in facilitating communication and decision-making within public administration.
